newsitem.title: USA: Colt's Manufacturing bids to buy big stake in Herstal.
newsitem.headline: Colt's Manufacturing bids to buy big stake in Herstal.

text.p: Colt's Manufacturing Co. said Thursday it has agreed to buy 92 percent of Herstal SA of Belgium in a deal that would unite two of the world's leading makers of handguns and other small-calibre arms.
Terms were not disclosed, but union sources at Herstal said Colt's had offered about $82 million for the stake.
French gun and arms maker Giat Industries said it has agreed to sell its 92 percent stake in Herstal to Colt's, which was founded in 1836 by Samuel Colt in Hartford.

Closely held Colt's said the acquisition would create one of the world's top makers of small-calibre arms, uniting its well-known Colt brand with the Herstal, Winchester and Browning names owned by the Belgian company.
Colt's said in a statement that the pact was subject to talks with the government of the Walloon region in Belgium, which owns the remaining 8 percent stake in Herstal.

Walloon Prime Minister Robert Collignon said Colt's would present a business plan in September. He said regional officials would accept the takeover if Herstal's activities were kept in Liege, where the company was founded in 1889.
Union officials in Belgium said they presented Collignon with an alternative plan that would turn Herstal around with the help of the government and private investors.
Herstal, founded in Liege near the Dutch border, has a strong position in the military market with FN Herstal and in the hunting and amateur shooting market with its Browning and Winchester brands.
Colt's was purchased in 1994 by an investor group led by Zilkha & Co., an investment bank.
